file_name: Lu et al. - 2009 - Improvement of a computer based surveyor training tool using a user centered approach.txt

barriers.description: Paper-based (low-fidelity) prototypes lacked sufficient detail to support quantitative evaluation, limiting the kinds of decisions designers could make from those tests.
barriers.justification: This methodological limitation hindered designers' ability to evaluate designs quantitatively and to make evidence-based decisions during iterative refinement (Evaluate designs and Integrate feedback & iteration workloads).
barriers.reference_excerpt: We also found, however, that paper-based prototypes may only be suitable for qualitative evaluations. They are lack sufficient detail to support quantitative decisions.

barriers.description: High-fidelity prototypes were relatively costly to develop, constraining the number of full-fidelity iterations designers could afford.
barriers.justification: The costliness of building high-fidelity prototypes limited the team's capacity to produce multiple detailed prototypes and run extensive iterative evaluations, hindering Produce design solutions and Evaluate designs workloads and slowing iterative refinement.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Unlike paper-based prototypes, it is relatively costly to develop high-fidelity prototypes. We suggest developers start from one high-fidelity prototype and revise it recursively based on the results of usability tests.
